#2424. What important features should you look for in a home security camera?

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (748 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

What important features should you look for in a home security camera?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When you're shopping for the best home gadgets, a lot of decisions tend to be based purely on budget or personal preferences.
  • With security cameras, though, your decisions can be deadly serious.
  • It has been revealed that I've tested or owned a number of security cameras for more than a decade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When you're shopping for the best home gadgets, a lot of decisions tend to be based purely on budget or personal preferences. No one needs an RGB lamp, for example, and an accessory that works with Google Home will usually function just as well paired with Amazon Alexa or Apple Home. There's a reason why Apple's new HomeView and HomePod mini 2 come in multiple colors — form might matter as much as function to some customers.

With security cameras, though, your decisions can be deadly serious. If a camera fails when you need it most, the results could be vandalism, property theft or yes, someone getting hurt or killed. Even your choice of doorbell camera matters, given the number of porch pirates out there.

It has been revealed that I've tested or owned a number of security cameras for more than a decade. At this point, I'm very familiar with the requirements for a great one. Just be warned that you may not be able to check off every item on your wishlist, especially if your goal is a security system that can operate 24/7, even when power or Wi-Fi goes out.

Industry observers note that when it comes to a camera's sensor, resolution isn't as crucial as you might think. 4K is nice to have — but more important than that is the device's night vision and field of view. The wider the view, the more a camera can potentially capture, with 180 degrees being ideal. As for night vision, you don't necessarily need color, but a sensor should be sensitive and sharp enough to clearly discern faces when little to no ambient lighting is available. I wouldn't buy a camera with less than 2K/1080p resolution and recommend searching online for real-world sample images.

Outdoor cameras should be fully water- and dust-resistant, with a rating of IP68 or better. Ensure the device's temperature limits are suitable to the climate you live in. Both wired and battery-powered cameras are potentially viable outside, but be aware that without a compatible solar panel, you're going to have to recharge batteries every six to 12 months at best. Actual runtime depends on factors like motion activity, signal strength and how often you check live feeds. You should be able to go at least a month between charges.

AI-based recognition of people, packages, animals and/or vehicles is sometimes crucial to avoiding a flood of generic motion alerts. That technology is often tied to both internet access and a subscription, though, so you might want to focus on models that handle recognition on-device at no extra charge. As subscription features go, cloud recording is more valuable. While local recording to an SD card is cheaper, it won't help you much if a thief steals or destroys your equipment.

Third-party platform support may also be vital. If you've already got one of Amazon's Echo Show or Fire TV devices in your home, for example, it only makes sense to pick up cameras with Alexa integration. You'll be able to check activity without pulling out your phone and set up camera-linked automations — for instance, triggering lights when motion is detected and you're away from home. Apple and Google offer similar hardware and software options. Note, however, that Apple Home can only be controlled using first-party hardware. That might make it a no-go if anyone in your home relies on an Android phone.

It has been revealed that if you're away often enough that someone might break in when power or internet access is down, search for battery-equipped cameras with cellular and SD card backup. This combination is going to be expensive, even before you factor in a monthly data initiative, but it's the only bulletproof solution. Alternately, you might invest in a Wi-Fi router with cellular backup and a whole-home battery solution, but the battery component alone will probably cost you thousands of dollars.

Industry observers note that the one remaining question is whether it's worth paying for professional monitoring. That's more subjective. Based on my own experience, the cost probably isn't worth it. All monitoring crews can do is call emergency services for you, and you might as well call the police yourself if you've received an intruder notification. There might be some value if you're regularly out of town for days or weeks at a time, as you're probably preoccupied, and you can't just dial 911 (or your regional equivalent) to reach the police in your hometown.

Fitbit Edge after 30 days: Life in the middle lane [Video]

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest compliment you can pay Google at the moment is that alongside the Pixel Watch, recent Fitbit releases have been a huge return to form – the Fitbit Edge included.
  • I need to nail my colors to the mast; I’m a Fitbit Air fanboy.
  • The Fitbit Edge worried me at first because it comes with a screen, which is something I realized isn’t that important to me day-to-day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest compliment you can pay Google at the moment is that alongside the Pixel Watch, recent Fitbit releases have been a huge return to form – the Fitbit Edge included.

I need to nail my colors to the mast; I’m a Fitbit Air fanboy. I’ve talked about it multiple times on the Pixelated podcast, here on the site, and it made me switch away from the Pixel Watch 5 because of how easily it fit into my existence without insisting on itself.

The Fitbit Edge worried me at first because it comes with a screen, which is something I realized isn’t that important to me day-to-day. After 30 days of wear, I’m conflicted because maybe I was too hasty to ditch a display on my wrist.

Recent findings suggest that the design is somewhat in a halfway house because it feels like it’s trying to be both a classic Fitbit while integrating some of the Pixel Watch features we know and love. Initially, I loved it, but it has become something that isn’t quite enough in either direction to suit my own tastes.

My love for the simplicity of the Fitbit Air has colored how I feel, but the Edge has an excellent core design. The display bezels remind me heavily of the original Pixel Watch; yes, they’re there, but you only notice them when the light catches the frame edge.

Sources indicate that after a month of daily wear, the display has lost a bit of its luster. The oleophobic coating is just about holding up, but now we’re into the cooler months; it’ll be put through a barrage of jacket cuffs and hoodie sleeves. This is one of the only durability concerns I have had so far.

Sources indicate that despite that admittedly minor concern, the Fitbit Edge is not something you need to baby. I’ve bashed it with weights, caught my wrist on zips (zippers for you, my American friends), and bashed it around with reckless abandon. It’s solid and hasn’t picked up as much as a single scuff. I don’t care too much if a fitness tracker gets a beating, whereas I would be more concerned about damaging my Pixel Watch.

Industry observers note that if you come in wanting a smartwatch-like experience from the Fitbit Edge, I think you’ll instantly be frustrated by the UI. It can feel cramped when you see notifications, and the large bezels don’t help all that much, but Google has well optimized almost all of the key sections outside of this.

Tiles are very well implemented; they’re just a smaller, squatter take on the Pixel Watch tile system, and it’s one of the best things about the Fitbit Edge interface. It’s also really snappy, which is something that isn’t the case with cheaper fitness trackers such as this. I’m constantly checking the weather or using the Google Health tile, but I have loved the quick access complication on the default watch face.

I tried a few of the other designs over the past 30 days; a lot of them are great. The default has become my favorite. It’s information-dense without being too overloaded. Tapping the complications takes you to the exact data point. I genuinely love how fuss-free an experience it is, save for a few minor complaints.

Recent findings suggest that we could criticize the accuracy of the data or the lack of tracking for certain types of workouts, but I think that misses the point of the Fitbit Edge. It’s a simple tracker with a screen, and the fact that you get even basic ECG on a device of this size is impressive.

I truly have worn the Edge daily for a full month, and while the bands are comfortable, I have found that they cause me to get a rash on the underside of my left wrist just under the palm. It’s actively stopping me from wearing it all the time now. I hope that the latest connector doesn’t slow down third-party development for bands, because I’m desperate for a fabric band to alleviate this problem.

This is exacerbated when the rubber band gets wet or sweaty. If you have sensitive skin, you might have the same problem as I have. Using some moisturizer has helped, but it is something I wasn’t prepared to suffer with before the Fitbit Edge turned up. I get that this is likely a “me” problem, but I wanted to note it.

When the screen gets wet or moist, it can bug out quite a lot. Taps don’t register properly, and a few water droplets can activate all the menus and submenus. Luckily, it won’t force your phone to place a call or anything like that, but the water protection mode is a must. I have kept it on extensively.

In a recent development, swimmers will probably get super frustrated; heck, I was on a rainy day as the screen kept bugging out. Overall, though, I have enjoyed the fitness tracking. Unlike on the Fitbit Air, it is nice to have a screen to start a workout rather than head over to my phone. That mentioned, the experience is the same as on your phone, but scaled down to fit the watch face.

Recent findings suggest that I dislike that you don’t get a phone notification to show the current workout progress by default, like the Fitbit Air. I had become accustomed to that. Luckily, you can enable it in the Google Health settings. I like having this as I forget to stop workouts so often without a prompt to hit “stop.”.

Sources indicate that with audio playback, you’re also getting the partial benefits of watch-phone controls, but it’s a two-step process unlike on Pixel Watch. You either have to go to the “Media” app or have the tile active and navigate to it to access play/pause and all your other streaming app controls. I tend not to bother using these as it’s finicky.

Industry observers note that this had me thinking about NFC. I think a lot of people would have liked NFC for Google Wallet on the Fitbit Edge, but I think having to enter a PIN on such a small screen would really have been a nightmare. I’ve made wireless payments with my watch less than five times, as it’s just easier to use my phone rather than contort my wrist to a wireless payment terminal. I figure this was something that was thought about and makes a lot of sense given the constraints.

Sources indicate that one of my other complaints is that the DND and Bedtime modes from my account haven’t synced or at least don’t appear to sync. Unless I’m mistaken, you need to activate these settings manually every time, which has been super annoying when in bed, as a flick of your wrist can blind you in a dark room. I figure this is something that can be fixed with an enhancement, so here’s hoping.

In a recent development, I’ve been super impressed with the battery life. A week is easily attainable for me with up to three gym visits per week, so I’ve charged 5 times in a month. That, to me, is excellent. I picked up a cheap charging dock, as the Edge uses the same charger for the Fitbit Air, so I figured why not.

It’s not the best-looking dock, but I quite like how it airs off my Edge so it’s not as stinky after gym sessions – as I wipe with an alcohol pad and clean as regularly as possible.

It has been revealed that the experience is fine; it’s almost a third of the price of the Pixel Watch and lacks a few features due to the various compromises – compromises I can deal with, as smartwatches have become information overload for me over time, and I like that the app selection is ultra-refined. At no point does the Fitbit Edge give you information overload.

Coming from a Charge 6 or an older Fitbit, this is an amazing replacement. It’s the new “default” fitness tracker for people who want all the hallmarks of what makes a great Fitbit.

Recent findings suggest that there is just enough. Nothing more, nothing less. To me, this feels like the perfect middle ground for a lot of people. You want something simple, touchscreen-enabled, and that doesn’t get in the way. As impressed as I have been with the Edge, though, I’ve loved a fuss-free tech accessory so much recently that I’ll probably go back to the Fitbit Air.

Siri Modular, the new Apple Watch face in watchOS 27, is gaining new style options. watchOS 27.3, right now in beta, adds two more style options to the existing set. This gives consumers five options for adjusting what type of information appears on Siri Modular.

Siri Modular originally shipped with three style options. Each supports a small line complication above the time.

Additionally, the original three styles include these options:.

In watchOS 27.3, Apple introduces two new Siri features that work with Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.

First, there’s Siri Recap which uses the Apple Watch to turn audio into high-level text summaries. Second, there’s Live Rewind which lets you view a transcript of the last 15 seconds of spoken word.

The two new Siri Modular Apple Watch face styles help surface three things: invoking Siri, viewing conversations with Siri, and viewing Siri Recaps on the Apple Watch.

The new styles include a pill-shaped module that includes icon shortcuts that go directly to Siri conversations, invoke Siri AI, or go directly to Siri Recaps in the Siri app.

Recent findings suggest that one style features a large digital clock with the new three-button Siri module. Another includes a compact digital clock with a Smart Stack tile and the new three-button Siri module.

This brings the style options to five. If you use the three circular complications configuration, you can also assign a Siri icon that invokes Siri AI.

watchOS 27.3 is currently in beta and expected to be released officially in December.

#2419. You can block AI slop and spam on these social media platforms

You can block AI slop and spam on these social media platforms

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (817 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some sites have started offering tools to filter the slop out of your feeds.
  • Recent findings suggest that these days, it's incredibly difficult to get away from the AI slop infestation thanks to it now flooding almost every social media platform.
  • Fortunately, social media platforms are beginning to allow users to decide how much AI-generated content gets to their feed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some sites have started offering tools to filter the slop out of your feeds.

Recent findings suggest that these days, it's incredibly difficult to get away from the AI slop infestation thanks to it now flooding almost every social media platform. And with each day that passes, it's becoming even harder to tell what is real and what came from a prompt, making the dead internet theory seem less far-fetched than it once did. The worst part is, users didn't exactly opt in to the AI-sloppification of their social media feeds.

Fortunately, social media platforms are beginning to allow users to decide how much AI-generated content gets to their feed. For now, though, most platforms only allow you to decrease how much AI content you see, not fully block it. There's also the fact that a 100 percent accurate block might not even be possible — social media platforms use labels and metadata to identify AI content, which can get lost when said content is edited or reuploaded.

As you'd expect, different platforms handle AI content differently. Some platforms including Pinterest, LinkedIn and TikTok allow you to reduce how much AI slop gets to your feed. Meanwhile, other platforms including Instagram, Facebook and YouTube have no dedicated setting, but there are workarounds that can filter out more AI content from your feed.

Currently, TikTok, Pinterest and LinkedIn are among the very few social media platforms that allow you to take control of how much slop gets shipped to your feed.

Select Refine your recommendations.

It has been revealed that in this menu, you can dial down AI-generated content in your Pinterest feed per category. Currently, the categories you can adjust include: Architecture, Art, Beauty, Entertainment, Fashion, Food & drink, Health, Home decor and Sport.

TikTok's AI slop setting is still in testing, so at the moment, it's not available to every user. To check if you're one of the lucky few:.

Go to your profile and tap the three-line menu icon at the top right corner.

Scroll down to Content Preferences.

In a recent development, in this menu, you'll see a bunch of sliders to control various types of content. Check for a slider related to AI-generated content, and move the slider left to reduce AI content to the minimum. If there's no dedicated AI content slider, then you'll have to wait for the feature to actually get released.

LinkedIn takes a platform-wide approach to curtailing AI slop and low-quality content. In July 2026, the platform introduced upcoming classifiers to identify and cut down the reach of AI slop posts. So you should already be seeing fewer AI slop posts in your LinkedIn suggested content recommendations from outside your network. If (or rather when) you come across AI slop posts on LinkedIn, you can use the "Seems like AI slop" button to report it. You'll find it in the three-dot menu on posts and comments. This won't necessarily affect the post's overall reach, but it'll ensure you see less of them and help train the classifier to identify AI slop better.

Industry observers note that platforms like Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and X (formerly Twitter) have no dedicated settings to block or reduce AI slop on your feed, but that doesn't mean you have take the slop sitting down. On these platforms, the best way to reduce AI slop is to intentionally train your algorithm to not recommend AI slop posts. Your social media algorithm is programmed to keep feeding you what you give attention to. So, the first step is to immediately skip any post that appears to be AI slop. Keep doing this and your algorithm will begin to pick up patterns in the type of posts you skip and start feeding less of them to you.

You can take this a step further by using each platform's feedback control to show you're not interested in that kind of content. For example, on Instagram when your feed indicates you a Reel you don't like, tap the menu icon at the bottom right and select "Not interested". On YouTube, use the three-dot menu beside videos to select "Not interested" and "Don't recommend channel". On X, tap the three-dot icon at the top right corner of a post, then select "Not interested in Post".

Sources indicate that you can also take more drastic measures and reset your recommendations entirely, and train your algorithm from a clean slate. On Instagram, go to your profile, tap the three-line menu icon, scroll down and tap "Content preferences" then select "Reset suggested content" and follow the prompts. On TikTok, navigate to Settings and privacy > Content preferences > Refresh your For You feed. On YouTube, you'll have to clear your watch history. Go to your profile page > History > tap the three-dot icon at the top right corner > Clear all watch history > Clear watch history.

  • And within hours of Monday's surprise announcement, senators set a date to question him in public — and under oath.
  • Huang, who co-founded chipmaker Nvidia, is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Thursday, Dec.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you thought the Jensen Huang saga was over when he stepped down as Nvidia's CEO, think again. Less than two weeks later, Nvidia gave him his job back.

And within hours of Monday's surprise announcement, senators set a date to question him in public — and under oath.

Huang, who co-founded chipmaker Nvidia, is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Thursday, Dec. 3, at 10 a.m. ET, just two days after he's scheduled to speak with various committees of the U.S. House of Representatives. He’s the only witness listed for the hearing, which will focus on U.S. rules limiting where companies can sell their most advanced AI chips. If you want to watch, the committee will be livestreaming the hearing on its website.

Huang has already returned to the Nvidia office, where he was welcomed by cheering employees.

"I'm going to be a better CEO the second time around," he told workers, as seen in a video on X.

Meanwhile, President Trump is taking personal credit for negotiating Huang's return to Nvidia. In a Truth Social post, the president stated he assured the Nvidia board that Huang did not pose a national security risk.

President Trump also posted a picture of Jensen Huang photoshopped into his assassination attempt scene while holding up a red bra with an Nvidia flag in the background. Yes, really.

It has been revealed that the questions about Nvidia's chips go back well before Huang initially stepped down. In 2024, federal investigators began looking into whether Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer based in Singapore, had sent advanced AI chips to China in violation of U.S. export rules. That investigation took on new significance when reports surfaced that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, who used to run Megaspeed. Jensen Huang acknowledged the affair, and U.S. authorities suspect Alice Huang of working for Chinese intelligence, according to the New York Times (though China has since denied that she was a spy).

Recent findings suggest that the newly empowered House Democrats also have questions for Huang, including whether Nvidia interfered with that investigation. In a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, they asked whether his department had allowed Nvidia to intervene in the Megaspeed probe. Lawmakers are also looking into exactly how Huang got his job back and what role the Trump administration played.

According to recent reports, just days before Nvidia brought him back, the board had made clear it had no plans to reinstate him, despite Huang saying he would be "honored" to return. On the company's earnings call on Nov. 17, board chair Harvey Jones even stated, "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

According to recent reports, yet, on Nov. 23, the board voted unanimously to do just that. In a statement, the board wrote that it had heard from senior U.S. officials, and "based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk.".

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Harvey Jones said in the statement.

Trump had already signaled he was open to Huang getting his job back. On Nov. 16, he told reporters he "would not mind" if Huang returned as CEO and stated Huang had "learned a substantial lesson.".

It has been revealed that by Monday, Trump was taking credit for the decision. He told CNBC he'd pushed Nvidia's board to bring Huang back. Asked whether the board would have done so without him, Trump remarked, "The answer is no. I believe my intervention was very vital." He also posted on Truth Social, writing, "The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World!".

Recent findings suggest that that leaves lawmakers in both parties asking what changed. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) called the decision "reckless" and asked the administration to name the officials who spoke to Nvidia and explain what they told the board. Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) asked, "No national security risk? Based on what?" he wrote on X.

In a recent development, huang had already agreed to answer questions from House lawmakers before he got his job back. That interview is still set for Tuesday, Dec. 1, two days before the public Senate hearing. He’ll meet with three House committees behind closed doors, and the interview will be transcribed.

Sources indicate that but now, Huang could also be answering a fresh set of questions in public about the affair that helped cost him his job and the president who says he got it back for him. So far, Nvidia and Trump have told their sides of the story. The hearing is a chance to hear Huang's.

iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (881 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it debuted in 2017.
  • Recent findings suggest that with iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch.
  • It has been revealed that the setup is simple.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it debuted in 2017. Tap your watch to compatible gym equipment, and Apple Watch shares your heart rate while the machine sends back metrics like distance, incline, pace, and calories.

Recent findings suggest that with iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch. I tested the new GymKit on iPhone and AirPods Pro 3 ($149, reg. $249) experience with a GymKit-compatible treadmill. It basically gives you the Apple Watch GymKit workout tracking experience, just without the watch. This could be useful in a lot of scenarios.

It has been revealed that the setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

In a recent development, once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

As a side note: Apple Watch has more accurate treadmill workout tracking as part of watchOS 27. GymKit remains the gold standard for accurate data, though.

GymKit also avoids two awkward gym habits. You don’t need to hold the treadmill’s metal heart-rate contacts while jogging. You also do not need to wear a Bluetooth heart-rate strap.

Recent findings suggest that airPods Pro 3 become the heart-rate source (and likely your podcast or music audio source as well). iPhone becomes the workout computer, which you can monitor during your workout. And the treadmill fills in the machine data while providing the surface for walking or running.

It has been revealed that apple has been moving more fitness features onto iPhone for years. iOS first made the Fitness app useful without Apple Watch as Apple Fitness+ leaned into iPhone as an entry point. AirPods Pro 3 pushed that further as the first AirPods with heart-rate tracking, after Apple tested the idea with Powerbeats Pro 2.

Sources indicate that iOS 27 brings those pieces together. GymKit on iPhone shouldn’t replace Apple Watch for people who wear one every day. Instead, it’s a great backup when your Apple Watch is dead, charging, or left at home.

It also gives iPhone and AirPods people a taste of the Apple Watch experience, which could attract future Apple Watch customers.

In testing with iOS 27 beta 1, my Exercise ring didn’t patch as I worked out without wearing Apple Watch. But after I put my watch back on, the Exercise ring caught up, and the workout appeared in Fitness with the right data.

My sample 16-minute treadmill walk showed 0.66 miles, 65 active calories, 97 total calories, 32 feet of elevation gain, and a 115 BPM average heart rate, just like if I’d worn an Apple Watch.

Sources indicate that I had been getting the impression that gym equipment manufacturers had been abandoning GymKit support - if they ever had done so initially. I even got the impression that the majority of equipment in Apple's own onsite Gym at the Apple Park may not have supported it - at least originally.

Does Apple have a webpage listing compatible brands and models? Like they do/did for HomeKit.

Sources indicate that what is other people perception? Any rowing machines that support it?

…checks - surprisingly it looks like Peloton do support it on their bikes.

According to recent reports, if I tried to use GymKit on iPhone without AirPods, the iPhone disconnected when the workout started because it had no heart-rate source. If I tried to start GymKit from iPhone while wearing Apple Watch, iOS pointed me back to the Workout app on Apple Watch instead, though you can continue without using the watch.

AirPods heart-rate permission also matters. You can manage it in Settings under your AirPods settings and privacy options. I had turned it off, mostly as a theoretical battery-saving move, but this test convinced me to turn it back on. AirPods Pro 3 can also work with Apple Watch to provide the best available heart-rate data.

GymKit on iPhone is one of those iOS 27 features that sounds small until it solves a real problem. If Apple Watch is your default workout tracker, it probably stays that way.

But if your watch dies or you forget it at home, iPhone plus AirPods Pro 3 can now log a treadmill workout with real heart-rate data and real treadmill metrics.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

That big catch is that its refresh rate only gets that high in HD mode.

I thought the refresh rate wars might slow down after displays hit 1,000Hz, but apparently I was wrong. That's because today Samsung confirmed the 27-inch, which is the world's first 1,100Hz gaming monitor.

The new Odyssey G6 is based on a dual mode IPS panel that supports two native resolutions: QHD (2,560 x 1,440) and HD (1,280 × 720). It also features decent brightness (400 nits typical), HDR10+ certification, a blistering gray-to-gray response time of just 1ms and compatibility with both AMD FreeSync Premium and NVIDIA G-Sync.

However, the big caveat with this display is that it can only reach its peak 1,100Hz refresh rate in HD mode, which means you can't enjoy its max resolution and max refresh rate at the same time. That stated, even in QHD mode, the panel can still hit 600Hz, which is higher than the vast majority of monitors on sale today.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, to help optimize the monitor's capabilities, the G60H also comes with Samsung's Odyssey Clear Motion tech, which uses a custom algorithm to help reduce blur and keep images looking as sharp as possible. There's also a black equalizer feature that automatically adjusts brightness levels in dark scenes to increase perceived contrast.

Recent findings suggest that the G6's stand is also height adjustable and supports swivel, tilt and pivoting, but stops short at being able to go all the way into portrait orientation. And while it won't show up on a traditional spec sheet, I appreciate that Samsung gave the monitor what it calls Auto Source Switch+, which allows the display to detect and switch over to new inputs as soon as they are plugged in without you needing to manually do it via the small joystick controls on the back of the panel.

Industry observers note that now it sort of goes without saying that if you are wondering what kind of people or games can actually utilize a panel this fast, then a monitor like this probably isn't for you. But for pro-level FPS players where every frame really does make a difference, this could deliver just a little bit of extra competitive advantage.

Unfortunately, official pricing and a release date for the Odyssey G6 G60H are still to be determined, but if you're in the market for an 1,100Hz monitor, you'll probably want to start saving up now as displays like this often go for around $1,000 or more.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Your Fire TV does this automatically, but you can force it if you're facing challenges.
  • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
  • Sometimes all you want is to sit down and decompress with a horrifyingly comic trip to Widow's Bay, but end up getting frustrated by a slow, buggy or unresponsive TV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your Fire TV does this automatically, but you can force it if you're facing challenges.

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Sometimes all you want is to sit down and decompress with a horrifyingly comic trip to Widow's Bay, but end up getting frustrated by a slow, buggy or unresponsive TV. If you're using an Amazon Fire TV or Amazon Fire TV Stick, that doesn't necessarily mean it's time to upgrade your device. Instead, you may simply be suffering from a storage concern.

Your Amazon Fire TV and Fire TV Stick may be slow because your cache is taking up too much storage. Essentially, these devices store information like your watch history and thumbnails in temporary files to make it easier and quicker to access when needed. Much like the web browser cache on your computer, this data is essential to keeping load times short and sweet.

Industry observers note that unfortunately, your Amazon Fire TV can suffer from too much of a good thing. Too many apps and shows can cause the cache to balloon, turning from a help into a hindrance. Unfortunately, you likely won't know you have crossed that threshold until it's too late. The solution isn't to limit your TV consumption, even if your health and attention span may thank you. Instead, dive into your Amazon Fire device's settings and clear its cache. The process is so easy that you should do it on all your streaming devices whenever you notice them slowing down.

If your device is running low on storage, Amazon may clear your cache for you. When your Fire TV is low on storage, it automatically clears the cache of apps you haven't used in the past 30 days. The feature is on by default and cannot be deactivated. But if you don't want to wait that long, you can force it by diving into your Fire TV's settings.

Recent findings suggest that luckily, clearing your cache manually is easy. To do so, open your Fire TV menu, go to Settings and select Applications. Next, choose Manage Installed Applications. From there, you can clear all your app caches by selecting Clear All Application Caches and then confirming your selection. If you would rather limit the action to a particular app,  select the app and choose Clear Cache. If you.

In a recent development, while clearing your cache can help, note that it isn't guaranteed to speed up your Fire TV immediately. Typically, it's a medium- to long-term solution, as your device will need to rebuild all the "shortcuts" that the cache provides. Thus, it may be a while before you see the full benefits of a cleared cache.

Recent findings suggest that beyond cache buildup, your device may also suffer from running outdated software. And while your Fire TV device should automatically download these updates when connected to the internet, it is always best to double-check that everything's up to date. To revision your Fire TV, return to your Fire TV menu and go to Settings. Next, navigate to My Fire TV or Device & Software > About > Check for System Update. This applies to apps as well.

You may also consider removing unused apps. Your Fire TV device has an Auto Offload feature that removes apps you haven't used in 30 days — crucially, without removing settings and login information, so you can easily pick up where you left off if you redownload. Although enabled by default, you may want to confirm Auto Offload is on by going to Settings > Applications > Auto Offload. You can also remove apps yourself by going to Settings > Manage Installed Applications. Once there, choose the app you want to offload, then press the Menu button. This can help if you want to fix app problems by uninstalling and then redownloading the app.

Industry observers note that another way to troubleshoot a slow Fire TV is the tried-and-true classic of turning it off and back on again. If even that doesn't help, you can go for the nuclear option and perform a factory reset.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

RCS is coming to GrapheneOS without Google Messages, as a proof-of-concept app demonstrates how the privacy-focused version Android can implement the messaging standard.

Sources indicate that as virtually all Android phones and now iPhone support RCS messaging, the standard is key to communication in 2026. But GrapheneOS owners, by default, are still stuck with SMS/MMS as RCS is typically locked behind Google Messages on Android.

It’s a problem that Graphene’s developers have been trying to work out for a while now, and it seems progress is being made. A proof-of-concept messaging app with RCS was shared on Twitter/X, showing Graphene’s RCS implementation working with both Google Messages and iOS with end-to-end encryption and full features including typing indicators and reactions.

Industry observers note that while this app skips the need to use Google Messages directly, the app does still use Google’s services as most carriers rely on Google for RCS. GrapheneOS still needs a sandboxed version of Google Play, for now, for this to work, but the developers say that a standalone version for carriers that support Google-less RCS will be coming.

We made a proof of concept RCS messaging app. It already has end-to-end encryption with MLS compatible with Google Messages and iOS, typing indicators, delivery/read receipts, reactions and media/file sharing. We'll use what was learned to integrate RCS into our Messaging app. pic.twitter.com/jzCTCCKrIQ.

There’s still no firm timeline for this newly introduced RCS support on GrapheneOS, but Google Messages can still be used in the meantime.

Since GTA 6 is not a multiplayer game, you might be able to play it without downloading the patch, but based on the patch notes, you will probably want to wait for it to install first.

It has been revealed that according to Rockstar's enhancement notes, the first GTA 6 patch is intended to fix seven common bugs players had encountered in the first few days after launch. Here are all the things Rockstar mentioned it fixed on Monday:.

"Several complications" that had caused the game to crash.

An problem that caused weather to not change for extended periods of time.

An problem where the game would not auto-save correctly.

"Several challenges" that caused in-game phone calls, including ones that push the story forward, to not trigger on time.

An issue where players could not lose their wanted levels.

An glitch where players could not deadlift at the gym.

An issue that caused partner characters to not hand bags of contraband to the player.

It has been revealed that as you can see, these range from minor irritations to nearly game-breaking glitches. Phone calls not triggering properly is especially bad, as they regularly unlock new story missions. Obviously, not being able to lose a wanted level would also be a pretty substantial bummer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Recorded Rides option is rolling out to Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis and St. Louis first.

Industry observers note that for riders looking for another layer of security, Uber is rolling out its new Recorded Rides feature. The latest feature on the ride-hailing app allows riders to opt for drivers who are using Uber's Record My Ride, an in-app function that uses the driver phone's selfie camera and microphone to record trips. Uber is starting the rollout with availability to Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis and St. Louis users first.

"Knowing a trip is being recorded can give riders and drivers greater peace of mind, encourage respectful interactions, and deter inappropriate behavior," Annie Duvnjak, Uber's global head of safety, said in a press release, adding that Recorded Rides will offer "greater confidence that a recording will be available if something doesn't go as planned.".

As for drivers, Uber remarked it's going to expand its Record My Ride feature, even testing out proactively enabling recording by default during late night trips or when picking up teen riders. Uber added that it's also looking into a function to turn on recording in emergency situations, like in cases that the app's RideCheck feature detects a possible car crash or if a trip is going "significantly off course." Uber will also test out having audio recording turned on by default during nighttime trips.

Industry observers note that drivers and riders still have the choice to opt out of any recordings within the app's settings. Duvnjak explained that "recordings are encrypted, stored on the user's device, and automatically deleted unless uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim," adding that Uber can only review recordings.

As the Recorded Rides feature starts its rollout, it's actually not the first time that Uber showed off in-app recording abilities. Earlier this year, Uber debuted a live video tool that lets parents or legal guardians monitor their teen's trip through the selfie cam on the driver's phone. Uber then expanded the feature with the Uber Kids program, that offers the same video feed for riders between 10 and 12 years old.

U.S. intelligence chief states more tech outages are inevitably coming

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (861 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that over the past month, tech outages have disrupted work emails, delayed bank transactions, and temporarily grounded departing flights across the United States.
  • On Sunday, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton remarked Americans should expect more disruptions like these, but not because of an incoming cyberattack; rather, because companies and government agencies are now in the process of updating aging technology.
  • Recent findings suggest that "We are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service," Clayton told CNN's State of the Union on Sunday, Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that over the past month, tech outages have disrupted work emails, delayed bank transactions, and temporarily grounded departing flights across the United States. Most of the biggest disruptions happened within six days of one another.

On Sunday, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton remarked Americans should expect more disruptions like these, but not because of an incoming cyberattack; rather, because companies and government agencies are now in the process of updating aging technology.

Recent findings suggest that "We are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service," Clayton told CNN's State of the Union on Sunday, Nov. 24. "That is going to happen." He noted much of the country's digital infrastructure was built over three decades or more and needs upgrades to run better and stay secure. (As one example, the FAA is still in the process of phasing out floppy disks, with a target of retiring the '90s-era technology by 2028.).

It has been revealed that clayton compared it to weekend maintenance at work: A manufacturer might take a system offline on Saturday and strategy to have it back by 2 A.M. Sunday. If the team finds another problem during the upgrade, it might be Sunday afternoon before the system is back up. "We are taking more systems down and putting them back up than ever before," he noted.

It was a lot to keep track of in six days: On Nov. 12, some Microsoft Outlook owners couldn't open their inboxes or send email. A day later, the Federal Aviation Administration paused departures nationwide after air traffic control communications problems. Then, on Nov. 16, a software bug delayed Chase transactions, and a separate outage briefly paused United Airlines departures. The following day, several Apple services ran into problems, and the National Security Agency's classified internal network went offline.

As Mashable has reported, despite the odd timing, the outages were not related, and Clayton told ABC's This Week that they were neither coordinated nor related to state-sponsored cyberattacks either. He attributed the disruptions to system upgrades he called "absolutely necessary going forward." "And we’re going to see more of that," he remarked. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

He also mentioned, "The need to improve our digital infrastructure is clear.".

It has been revealed that AI is identifying zero-day bugs in software faster than ever, and fixing those flaws safely takes time. Some zero-day bug bounty programs have been forced to shut down entirely, and earlier this year, the Zero Day Initiative reported bug reports had increased 490 percent year over year. Companies now have to move quickly to patch all the new bugs found by AI.

Microsoft President Brad Smith called the pressure to move faster part of the "AI ripple effects" on CBS's Face the Nation on Nov. 22 — companies want to fix flaws before attackers can use them. On older systems, Smith remarked, moving that rapidly can leave engineers with less time to test what happens when a fix goes live.

Sources indicate that dmitri Alperovitch, chair of the Silverado Policy Accelerator, described what that looks like for the people doing the work. "I.T. teams, network teams are overwhelmed. They're working 24/7. They're making mistakes," he noted on the same program. He expects more outages as teams work through the growing number of flaws they've found.

Industry observers note that the National Security Agency's outage offers one example of how an urgent fix can disrupt service. The agency's classified internal network went offline on Nov. 17 during work after the agency installed a security fix for PHP, a widely used programming language, Clayton told Fox Business. Those same flaws, known as P2PSHELL, had already forced some website operators to take their sites offline in October while they installed the fix, as Mashable reported at the time. OpenAI noted that its GPT-5.6 Sol model had found the bugs.

Sources indicate that microsoft, on the other hand, traced its outage to a software bug introduced in July that went unnoticed for months. It only became a problem in November, when Microsoft sent more Teams traffic to servers that also handle Outlook email. Some of those servers were already offline, and the extra traffic triggered the bug on others. When those servers stopped responding, Microsoft automatically sent traffic to the ones that were still working. They started to fail, too.

Smith mentioned the broader work could take months. His advice? Everyone should install security updates as soon they arrive on a phone or laptop.

From Amazfit and RingConn to Samsung, these alternatives offer different ways to avoid Oura's recurring fees.

According to recent reports, oura's Ring 5 starts at $399, but that's just the hardware. To get detailed sleep, recovery and health insights, you'll need to pay $5.99 per month or $69.99 a year for a membership. Without that subscription, you can only get three scores per day: Sleep, Activity and Readiness. With two years of membership, the base ring costs almost $539 before taxes, so it's a pretty expensive health tracker that can't even tell time.

In a recent development, as we mentioned in our Oura Ring 5 review, there's still a lot to love about its slimmer design and weeklong battery life. However, some competitors monitor similar health data without the monthly fee, and others are much cheaper. We compared their current US prices, included features and independent reviews to see where those savings come with compromises.

In a recent development, the Amazfit Helio Ring is priced around $161, significantly lower than Oura's entry-level ring. It monitors sleep, heart rate and recovery via the Zepp app, which can also integrate data from an Amazfit smartwatch. Helio owners can right now get Zepp Aura Premium for free. There are some obvious compromises, though. The ring is only available in sizes 8, 10 and 12, and Amazfit rates battery life at up to four days. So while the price is tempting, it's only worth it if one of those sizes fits you.

Another budget-friendly choice is Renpho's LYNX, which is $179.99 on sale from $199.99. It comes with a portable charging case, is compatible with iOS and Android and can monitor sleep, stress and activity, without needing a subscription. Unfortunately, hands-on testing has shown that the heart-rate data were not consistent during exercise, and sleep data were questionable too. Its app also provided little analysis of the data it gathered, so the savings are harder to appreciate when you're second-guessing the readings.

In a recent development, the RingConn Gen 2 Air is priced at $199 and is stated to last up to 10 days on a single charge, with heart rate, skin temperature and sleep monitoring without any additional fees. It comes with a charging dock rather than a portable battery case, while sleep apnea pattern monitoring is reserved for pricier RingConn models. If you're only interested in tracking your sleep without an additional monthly charge, those may be acceptable compromises.

Sources indicate that samsung's Galaxy Ring, which we found somewhat basic and a bit pricey in our Galaxy Ring review, has a list price of $399.99, though Amazon has it right now listed for $324.99. The savings are down the road though, as Samsung doesn't charge a membership fee for its health-tracking features. It also comes with a charging case, as mentioned in our roundup of fitness trackers with no subscription fees. The issue is that it's Android-only and some Galaxy AI features require a compatible Samsung Galaxy phone, so iPhone owners can cross this one off their lists.

The Circular Ring 2 is priced at $349 and includes single-lead ECG readings, heart-rhythm monitoring and sleep tracking without requiring a subscription, though some advanced features demand an additional fee. Despite the impressive hardware, the software does leave a lot to be desired. Reviewers have found the app cluttered and slow to sync, though Circular has since released updates addressing connectivity challenges. The firm also cautions that its health measurements aren't intended for medical diagnosis.

According to recent reports, lastly, the Ultrahuman Ring Pro is more expensive than Oura at $479. It comes with a charging case and free core health tracking, but some optional PowerPlugs cost extra. In our Ring Pro review, we noted that the detailed app and the battery life of about 10 days were good, but automatic workout detection sometimes failed to capture workouts. There's also legal uncertainty: Oura sued Ultrahuman again in October 2026, seeking to block US sales of the Ring Pro. An earlier patent ruling had already blocked imports of the Ring Air.

For a pair of third-generation earbuds, you'd imagine (or at least hope for) major upgrades. Nothing delivered in a few areas where we were looking for improvements. What's more, the Nothing Ear 3 introduces a new way to interact with the device and its case.

Before we get too ahead of ourselves, there's a pair of Black Friday deals for the Nothing Ear 3 that drop them by almost 40%.

The Nothing Ear 3 continues the classic Nothing transparent design with longer battery life, redesigned audio drivers, and support for LDAC hi-res audio. The Ear 3 introduced an aluminum case with a dual-microphone system.

If you prefer, you can also find these deals on Nothing's U.S. website during its Black Friday sale.

These earbuds are ✅ recommended if you value a device that won't drop out on you. The Nothing Ear 3 battery life is a major highlight. Compared to the Ear 1 and Ear 2, the Ear 3 delivers roughly 5.5 hours of listening time per bud (Adaptive ANC enabled). This jumps to 10 hours if you disable ANC, which just means more tunes or podcasts or demonstrates/movies. Another interesting feature with the Ear 3 is Super Mic. It is a dual-microphone system in the charging case. Pressing the TALK button switches audio from your earbuds to your case—more on this in a moment.

In a recent development, however, you should probably ❌ skip this deal if you need earbuds with more reliable ANC/transparency modes. The Ear 3 falls kind of flat in these areas, leaving you wanting more. What's more, while we've praised the upgraded battery life, the Ear 3 isn't for you if you want great audio and long battery life. That sounds like a no-brainer, right? If you want LDAC audio and ANC, your battery life drops to ~3.5 hours per bud.

Recent findings suggest that super Mic is the massive new thing for the Nothing Ear 3. Press the TALK button to switch your audio output to the case. This is intended for consumers on calls or taking a voice memo. One thing that we noted in our review is that the Ear 3 flips the switch on a classic sentiment. Wireless earbuds aren't renowned for "great" mics. However, with the dual microphone system in the case, it offers something with more substance.

The redesigned 12mm drivers are also a high point for the Ear 3. Factor in its LDAC audio support and you've got a pair of buds that are pretty handy. What's more, its original starting price wasn't terrible compared to the competition. Since it's Black Friday, that price is even more attractive if you're looking for a new pair.

Recent findings suggest that the patch appears to be centered on web-only instances of Google Meet, and might not include the app on Android or iOS. For the time being, those versions may still be limited to streaming in 720p for those who don’t have an active Google One subscription.

Google Meet started its extended rollout of 1080p streaming to everyone earlier this month, so it shouldn’t be much longer until the change has taken place completely.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alarms are one of the most important iPhone features, and iOS 27 offers a key feature that should help your alarm actually wake you: a new volume setting for alarms that’s independent of other volume settings.
  • Sources indicate that have you ever accidentally slept through an alarm?
  • Industry observers note that I suspect that’s a pretty common reason for missed alarms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alarms are one of the most important iPhone features, and iOS 27 offers a key feature that should help your alarm actually wake you: a new volume setting for alarms that’s independent of other volume settings.

Sources indicate that have you ever accidentally slept through an alarm? We’ve all done it. And most often for me, it’s because my alarm volume was unintentionally set to a very low level.

Industry observers note that I suspect that’s a pretty common reason for missed alarms. And in iOS 27, Apple finally has the fix—but it requires manually setting up.

Inside Settings ⇾ Sounds & Haptics, you can now set a volume for alarms that’s independent from the systemwide ringtone setting.

It has been revealed that iOS 27 has two new sections in this Settings screen: Alarms and Timers, and Alerts and System Sounds. Both include ‘Match Ringtone Volume’ toggles that are on by default. This means your volume for alarms, timers, alerts, and other system sounds are all determined by the ringtone volume.

But if you disable the Alarms and Timers toggle, you’ll get a latest volume slider that applies only to those system functions, and won’t be impacted by your ringtone volume.

As seen above, this means you can crank the Alarms and Timers volume up to the maximum level without making every other system sound, including notifications and phone calls, be similarly deafening.

So the next time you sleep through your alarm, it won’t be because the alarm was too quiet.

In case you missed it, iOS 26 introduced a welcome feature that lets you set custom snooze durations for alarms, and also an option to have alarms trigger on your iPhone even if you’re wearing an Apple Watch.

Do you initiative to set a custom volume setting for alarms in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that nvidia finance chief Colette Kress led the firm for 11 days during Jensen Huang's sudden but brief departure.
  • The 59-year-old Kress at the moment has roughly 4.775 million shares directly and indirectly held, which makes her worth approximately $778 million at Monday's market close.
  • The 63-year-old Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital relationships, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that nvidia finance chief Colette Kress led the firm for 11 days during Jensen Huang's sudden but brief departure. When Nvidia's board officially reinstated Huang as CEO on Monday, the company also unveiled that Kress would continue in her role as CFO.

The 59-year-old Kress at the moment has roughly 4.775 million shares directly and indirectly held, which makes her worth approximately $778 million at Monday's market close.

The 63-year-old Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital relationships, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy.

Nvidia stock soared 31% and the Nasdaq surged more than 6% Monday after the organization announced that Huang would return as CEO, president and board director, effective immediately. Huang returned to the office Monday to crowds of Nvidia employees cheering his return.

Kress, who stepped in as interim CEO during Nvidia's moment of crisis, joined the chipmaker as finance chief in September 2013 following stints at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments.

Sources indicate that as CFO, Kress oversees the balance sheet of a company aggressively financing many of the infrastructure deals that power the artificial intelligence buildout. Those agreements also raise concerns over circular financing and Nvidia's AI exposure in the event of a slowdown.

In the first earnings call after Huang's resignation, Kress sought to reassure investors, raising the firm's fiscal 2028 revenue-growth forecast to roughly 75% from 70%.

She told analysts during a Q&A portion that it was "business as usual" at the organization. She later told CNBC's Jim Cramer that customers have stood by the chipmaker and that demand continues increasing.

"The board has determined that they will not reinstate Jensen, and that is our statement and what the board has decided to do," Kress said.

During the company's first all-hands meeting after Huang's resignation, Kress also struck an optimistic tone, telling employees to "move forward" and mentioning pay raises.

According to recent reports, but Kress didn't manage to impress many market participants and insiders, who compared the interim chief to Huang. Last week, the stock recorded its worst week and longest weekly losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis as AI stocks plummeted.

It has been revealed that "She just wasn't him," The Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman told CNBC. "I think she would have had to strengthen her bench around her a lot, because you have a visionary, product technology driven CEO that was literally the epicenter of the tech giant. He was the entire identity.".

One person CNBC spoke with remarked Kress handled the situation with "skill and grace" while managing a tough job.

The former Nvidia employee, who asked not to be named because the matter is private, stated Kress helped reassure the industry and that people should not be so "quick to rush to judgment.".

In the week since Huang's exit, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang belittled Kress, calling her "a deer in the headlights.".

Huang mentioned in the press release announcing his return that he was "grateful" for Kress "leading NVIDIA during this period.".

However, Poehler and Schur's collaboration isn't the only spark of Parks and Recreation magic you'll find in Dig. In a blink-and-you'll-miss-it moment, Dig also features a cameo from none other than Rashida Jones, who plays Leslie's best friend, nurse Ann Perkins, in Parks and Recreation.

Industry observers note that jones' appearance occurs in episode 5, when she pops up as a woman taking a photo of archaeologists Elise (Poehler) and Neville (Hugh Laurie) at a beachside restaurant. My Parks-loving self has never rewound a scene so fast to make sure my eyes weren't deceiving me.

It has been revealed that according to Schur, the cameo came about due to proximity. Dig shot in Italy and Greece, and Jones is semi-permanently located in London. Schur, Poehler, and Jones, who have been friends since even before working together on Parks and Recreation, were communicating with one another during production.

"We were just texting with [Jones], and we were like, 'It's not that long a flight. What if you just hopped over here and hung out with us at this hotel we're staying at?'" The highlight of the scene comes right after Jones exits, when Elise casually remarks, "She's very pretty.".

It's a sweet reminder of one of TV's most enduring female friendships, and it's right at home in Dig, which is full of sweet female friendships in its own right. "It was a very smart little mini gift to the folks who were fans of that show who will enjoy seeing them back together again," Schur said.

“I spoke to them, let me put it that way … And I convinced them,” the president told CNBC.

Huang was forced to step down from his role as CEO, which he held for 33 years, after news broke that he had affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including a direct report.

According to recent reports, “President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung told Semafor.

While Trump has declared that Huang “did absolutely nothing wrong,” many government officials aren’t buying the president’s point of view. Huang is still expected to testify in closed-door conversations with three committees of the House of Representatives on December 1. He is also slated to appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify publicly, though that hearing has not been scheduled yet.

In a recent development, “People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it’s a threat to lose him,” Trump noted to CNBC.

Recent findings suggest that trump has maintained this position through the scandal, even denying that he was ever told about Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang (no relation). The New York Times reported, on the contrary, that Trump’s secretary of state and national security adviser Marco Rubio briefed him aboard Air Force One in May.

Earlier this spring, Rubio also supervised the drafting of a memo that circulated among top policymakers, warning that Alice Huang was spying for China’s Ministry of State Security.

#2388. Breaking: How to connect your Bluetooth headphones to your Xbox Series X

Breaking: How to connect your Bluetooth headphones to your Xbox Series X

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (491 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since the Xbox Series consoles lack support for Bluetooth headphones, here's how you can work around the problem.
  • Having the best audio can elevate any game, and sometimes TV speakers just don't cut it.
  • According to recent reports, the problem with using even the best wireless Bluetooth headphones for gaming is latency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since the Xbox Series consoles lack support for Bluetooth headphones, here's how you can work around the problem.

Having the best audio can elevate any game, and sometimes TV speakers just don't cut it. But while Bluetooth headphones are supported on virtually every device from smartphones to laptops, the same isn't true of game consoles. Out of the box, an Xbox Series X can't connect directly to Bluetooth headphones, but there are a few workarounds if you want to get more out of your game's sound than your TV can provide.

According to recent reports, the problem with using even the best wireless Bluetooth headphones for gaming is latency. Sending audio over Bluetooth introduces a tiny delay before your headphones actually receive it. Most of the time, that's not an matter, but when your game's sound is even a fraction of a second off, it can be distracting. Worse, it can make rhythm games that rely on audio cues nearly unplayable. If you do want wireless audio from your Xbox Series X, there are a few solutions, but none are perfect.

One simple but costly route is to buy the official Xbox Wireless Headset, which retails for $120. Microsoft uses its own wireless standard for these headphones to connect with extremely low latency, and since Bluetooth isn't an option, you have to pay more for the first-party version if you want wireless audio. Some third-party manufacturers like Audeze and SteelSeries also make Xbox-compatible wireless headsets, but they can be just as expensive as Microsoft's version or more. Third-party headsets that support Xbox's wireless protocol need to be licensed by Microsoft, and you'll see the Xbox logo on the box.

According to recent reports, another option is to route Bluetooth audio through an adapter or your TV. Some Bluetooth adapters are made to plug into the Xbox controller's headphone jack and transmit the audio coming through it, while others connect to the console's USB port and transmit from there. Higher-end headphones like the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite that come with a dedicated low-latency dongle are the best choice for sound quality, but they also tend to be more expensive. If you already own a smart TV that can transmit a Bluetooth signal, you can also set your console to output to the TV, then connect it to your headphones. Any of these options will be cheaper than buying an entirely new set of headphones.

Sources indicate that the cheapest way to connect your headphones to your Xbox Series X is just to use the controller's audio jack as it's intended. Some Bluetooth headphones include a jack and audio cable as a wired backup, but that's not always the case. If you have any headphones that support wired connections, though, using the controller jack is the best way to avoid latency. It's not actually wireless, of course, but connecting your headphones to the controller won't compromise your audio quality.

Right from the moment Peacock's Dig was revealed, comparisons to Parks and Recreation felt inevitable.

Industry observers note that the latest sitcom reunites Parks and Recreation's co-creator Mike Schur with the show's leading lady, Amy Poehler. As co-creators on Dig, the two once more deliver a workplace comedy about a competent, passionate leader, played by Poehler, who assembles a motley team. In Dig's case, that's archaeologist Elise, who's overseeing a Grecian archaeological dig site.

Comparison to a prior project is territory Schur and Poehler know well, dating back to the first days of Parks and Recreation.

Sources indicate that "When we started Parks and Rec, we were compared to The Office, because The Office was such a big deal at the time," Schur told Mashable over Zoom. "That was sort of our mini obstacle we had to get through.".

Both indicates were workplace-set mockumentaries on NBC. Critics and viewers alike were quick to call out the similarities.

While talking with Steve Carell for an episode of Good Hang earlier this year, Poehler recalled, "Parks and Rec had the worst launch ever. Everyone was like, 'This is not The Office. We don't like this.'".

Recent findings suggest that however, Parks and Recreation ditched Office-like cynicism in favor of a warmer tone, and it carved out a niche of its own. Still, for Schur, comparisons to The Office prepared him for how people might react to his later work. That includes Dig.

"[With Dig,] we're being compared to a different show that we also made," Schur remarked. "We're experienced with the concept that people have expectations for something going in. And we're a little bit older and wiser in terms of how we manage that emotionally.".

While some might say that comparison is the thief of joy, Schur has found the upside.

"I think it's a position of privilege to be in, to have a show that people are like, 'I hope it's like this other thing you did,'" Schur stated. "That's great, because that means people watched the first one and cared about it. So I hope that people will watch this latest show and judge it on its own merits.".

Global climate negotiations fell apart as delegates tried to tackle AI’s growing carbon footprint.

Global climate negotiations fell apart as delegates tried to tackle AI’s growing carbon footprint.

According to recent reports, if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

According to recent reports, the clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It’s a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday.

In a recent development, each year, attendees try to make good on the commitment to stop climate change as part of the 2015 Paris climate accord. Preventing extreme weather from growing more terrifying, coastal communities from flooding, and droughts from wrecking food and water systems requires slashing greenhouse gas emissions. But in order to power homes or cars with solar and wind instead of oil and gas, they need to go electric.

“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this”.

To that end, one of the most anticipated outcomes of this year’s negotiations was a deal to raise electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, compared to about 20 percent today. That becomes harder to do, however, when data centers are causing electricity demand to skyrocket. That made the rush of fresh AI data centers a climate concern alongside talks on how to transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy.

In a recent development, “Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this, and it will inevitably come up in the discussions. It’s part of the broader energy transformation,” Chris Bowen, Australia’s minister for climate change and energy and the president of COP31 climate negotiations, told Politico in an interview at the start of the COP31 summit.

Despite becoming the longest COP yet, with debates lasting two days longer than scheduled, official negotiations fell apart spectacularly. Delegates ultimately failed to garner enough support to pass the “pact” they’d been bargaining on for two weeks. The EU, UK, and several smaller nations most vulnerable to climate change rejected the deal that they saw as too weak. The pact omitted the term “fossil fuels” despite many nations calling for stronger commitments to phase out oil, coal, and gas. And the US, the epicenter of the data center buildout and the biggest climate polluter historically, was a no-show after the pro-fossil-fuel Trump administration pulled the country out of the Paris accord (twice).

With official negotiations falling apart, and countries only making voluntary commitments on AI and electrification, some environmental and humanitarian groups called this year “the worst COP” ever.

It has been revealed that to meet the Paris goals, nations will need to cut their greenhouse gas emissions roughly in half by 2030 before reaching net zero by the middle of the century. Many tech companies made similar commitments in recent years, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta. But thanks to the AI boom, those goals have fallen by the wayside.

It has been revealed that meta is “re-evaluating” its timeline to reach net zero emissions as it focuses on AI, the firm said in its annual sustainability report on Thursday. Meta reported a 45 percent year-over-year increase in climate pollution. Google’s and Microsoft’s carbon footprints are also growing despite climate commitments the companies have made. Data centers’ electricity consumption is forecast to double by 2030, according to a forecast by the International Energy Agency.

“That is a huge climate risk: rising power demand from data centres is not yet sustainable, and an AI boom cannot be allowed to become a fossil fuel boom,” Bruce Douglas, CEO of the Global Renewables Alliance, tells The Verge in an email. Data centers were “a key topic” at COP31, according to Douglas, whose organization cohosted a panel on the challenges during the event.

In the US, the country with the most data centers, power sector emissions could increase 42 percent by 2030 as energy companies build more fossil fuel infrastructure to meet data center electricity demand, according to a recent analysis by the Sierra Club. Already, hyperscale data centers in the US create more climate pollution than the country of Denmark, a separate study by Harvard researchers recently found.

In a recent development, to stop data centers from creating more pollution, they would need to be powered by additional new sources of renewable energy, Douglas says. He adds that data centers are currently competing with everyone else for grid connections, finance, and electricity generation capacity — and against arguably more essential tasks like heating and air conditioning, as well as electrifying transportation.

It has been revealed that many tech companies match their electricity use with renewable energy purchases. But unless they’re helping to build fresh sources of green energy to meet their added electricity demand, they might just end up hogging limited renewable energy capacity. And if more fossil fuels make up the difference, then greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise overall.

“Should upcoming green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?”.

Industry observers note that “In many cases, datacentres are outbidding other consumers to get speed to power,” Douglas says. “Should newly introduced green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?”.

There was some progress. Around 80 nations signed onto a voluntary pledge to increase electricity’s share of energy consumption to 35 percent over the next decade, according to COP31 president Murat Kurum. The list of countries that includes, however, hasn’t been published yet, Carbon Brief reports.

Another voluntary pledge to keep AI from derailing climate action by calling on data centers to run on less polluting energy also failed to garner much support. Douglas notes that by using the term “low-emission energy,” the pledge still leaves the door open for natural gas (which produces less carbon pollution than coal when burned but is a significant source of methane pollution) to keep powering data centers.

According to recent reports, “The Antalya A.I. pledge is a step in the right direction to address an vital piece of the impacts, but needs teeth in order to translate into stronger protections for people and the planet,” the nonprofit Natural Resources Defense Council noted in a statement when the pledge was first confirmed. “The speed, scale and scope of this challenge is bigger than perhaps anything before it, and the guardrails must be commensurate.”.
